purpose: One closed-loop task, four existing controller/observer pairs, equal bounded design budget, train/validation lock then independent test; no global optimum or hardware claim

sensorFixture.scope: Same test injection amplitudes in all cases; calibration estimator sees readings only. Colored noise and actuator/model mechanisms remain as declared by scenario.

theoryDesign.terminal: full nominal discrete Riccati for each actual Qc/Rc
theoryDesign.note: Qc_i=1/stateScale_i^2 and Rc=effortMultiplier/forceScale^2. Scales are declared engineering design choices, not identified physical values or safety bounds.

task.score: Mean of declared normalized tracking, upright-angle, effort and command-increment squared costs. Evaluate x_k/u_k; first delta-u is from zero. Failed/partial runs receive no full-duration score.
task.timingScope: Host construction/solve/observer/full-step measurements reported separately. Not used to choose a stochastic timing winner or claim WCET/sensor-to-hardware admission.

selection.order: hard failure count, final-task failure count, mean score for full-completed sets, exact ties prefer baseline then fixed candidate ID
selection.crossPairRule: Among validation-eligible pairs within 1% of minimum validation score, choose fixed lower simplicityOrder. It is a policy, not proof of algorithm dominance.
selection.testRule: Lock one candidate per pair and one recommended pair BEFORE test. Report baseline and selected for every pair. Test can reject the locked recommendation but cannot select another one.
selection.adoptionScope: Optional manual application to the declared simulation task only; all primary cases must meet task, no candidate-only primary task failure, and mean primary task score <=1.02*same-pair baseline if both complete. Boundaries do not expand admission.

claims: This finite 2-parameter grid is an interpretable joint design search, not a globally optimal co-design or complete identification.
Qc shape, horizon, P0 and measured Re are fixed. Varying Qe is an effective task-tuning choice and is not labelled calibrated physical noise.

LQR has force clipping and common physical rail/angle evaluation; MPC additionally enforces nominal predicted rail/input constraints. Both use same task and nominal model, but their optimization formulations differ.
Truth is used only for simulated task evaluation; no controller or observer receives it.
Every candidate gets the same training cases; selection does not inspect test data or timing measurements. New tests are held out only for this first study, then become regression data.
A validation winner failing admission is retained as a rejected result, not replaced by the best test performer.
